core_obligations: Replace X by its smooth locus U, nonempty by hypothesis and therefore dense and scheme theoretically dense, and observe that this property survives base change to the algebraic closure so that it suffices to treat U (proof lines 4783-4787).
Show U is geometrically connected because it carries a rational point (proof lines 4788-4789).
Show the base change of U is reduced and normal because U is smooth, and conclude that it is integral since it is connected, normal and Noetherian (proof lines 4790-4794).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the smooth locus (proof lines 4783-4787).
Geometric connectedness from the rational point (proof lines 4788-4789).
Reduced and normal plus connected gives integral (proof lines 4790-4794).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a variety over k possessing a k-rational point at which it is smooth is geometrically integral (statement lines 4775-4780). The proof replaces X by its smooth locus U, which is nonempty, hence dense and scheme theoretically dense, and remains dense and scheme theoretically dense after base change to the algebraic closure; it therefore suffices to prove geometric integrality of U (proof lines 4783-4787). There the rational point makes U geometrically connected, while smoothness makes the base change reduced and normal, and a connected normal Noetherian scheme is integral, which finishes the argument (proof lines 4788-4794). The claim is H2: three standard inputs combined in a short argument, with the reduction to the smooth locus as the step that makes the geometric connectedness hypothesis available.
